ORVEXA - The Future of Astronaut Health

We are ORVEXA, a team passionate about space exploration, science, and innovation.

Our goal is to develop an intelligent health monitoring solution designed to support astronauts throughout space missions. By combining technology, data analysis, and biomedical research, we aim to help monitor vital signs, identify potential health risks, and improve astronaut well-being.

details:
ORVEXA — The Future of Astronaut Health

The Problem

Human spaceflight presents significant challenges to the health and physical condition of astronauts. During long-duration missions, microgravity and the demanding conditions of the space environment can affect cardiovascular function, muscle strength, bone health, sleep patterns, and overall physical performance.

Monitoring these changes is important because even relatively small changes in an astronaut’s condition can influence daily activities, physical performance, and mission readiness. However, health information needs to be organized and presented in a clear and accessible way to support consistent observation and better awareness of potential concerns.

Our Solution

ORVEXA is a desktop-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to help organize, record, and review important physiological and well-being indicators.

The application provides a structured environment where users can enter health measurements, monitor changes over time, review recorded information, and explore personalized health-related insights. Instead of presenting all information in one place, ORVEXA organizes its functionality into dedicated sections, making health monitoring more understandable and accessible.

Key Features

  • Health Data Monitoring: Users can record resting heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, fatigue level, and reported discomfort.
  • Personal Baseline Tracking: The application allows users to record a reference heart rate baseline and compare it with subsequent measurements.
  • Measurement History and Trends: Recorded measurements can be stored and reviewed to observe changes over time.
  • AI-Assisted Health Insights: An optional AI assistant can analyze entered measurements, answer health-related questions, and generate draft exercise recommendations.
  • Exercise Support: ORVEXA includes exercise concepts involving equipment such as ARED and CEVIS, with activities organized around strength, cardiovascular conditioning, and recovery.
  • Safety-Oriented Checks: Built-in validation and conservative safety rules can flag unusual readings or reported symptoms and pause automatic exercise recommendations when additional medical review is needed.
  • Data Storage and Reports: Measurements and analysis records are stored locally in an SQLite database, with report export support.

Why ORVEXA Matters

The purpose of ORVEXA is to make astronaut health information easier to organize, understand, and review. By bringing several health indicators and monitoring functions into one application, the project demonstrates how a structured digital tool could support health awareness during space missions.

The project is particularly relevant to long-duration missions, where maintaining physical condition and monitoring changes in human physiology are important aspects of crew health and mission preparation.

Technology and Implementation

ORVEXA is developed in Python using PySide6 for its desktop interface and SQLite for local data storage. It also supports optional AI connectivity through OpenAI or a locally hosted Ollama model.

The application is an independent research and demonstration prototype. Measurements are entered manually by the user. It does not directly connect to spacecraft sensors, NASA systems, or live astronaut medical databases, and it is not a certified medical diagnostic system.

Future Potential

Future development could explore integration with validated spaceflight research datasets, additional physiological indicators, wearable monitoring devices, and more advanced health trend analysis. These improvements could help expand ORVEXA into a more comprehensive astronaut health monitoring concept.
